# ceblar-20 v0.4

## Overview

v0.4 establishes the first verified ring-3 userspace foundation for **ceblar-20**, a freestanding 32-bit x86 educational kernel. The release boots through GRUB Multiboot2, initializes protected-mode segmentation and paging, creates isolated per-process address spaces, loads an embedded ELF32 image, and enters ring 3 through a real `iret` transition.

## Included functionality

The release includes the Multiboot2 boot path, GDT and TSS setup, IDT/PIC/ISR infrastructure, a bitmap physical-memory manager, identity paging, address-space creation and destruction, PMM-backed user stack mapping, a first-fit kernel heap, VGA and serial output, keyboard input, PIT timer uptime and sleep, a modular driver registry, a minimal VFS, thirteen syscall slots, an ELF32 `PT_LOAD` mapper, eager page-by-page fork cloning, and the corrected `pusha`-compatible interrupt-frame ABI.

The embedded user image performs `SYS_WRITE` through `INT 0x80`. The output is written by the kernel’s serial-backed VFS path and returns safely to ring 3, demonstrating a complete kernel/user syscall round trip.

## Verification

```sh
make clean
make -j2
grub-file --is-x86-multiboot2 build/kernel.elf
make test
make size
```

The expected serial markers include:

```text
gdt: initialized successfully
tss: initialized successfully
pmm: total pages ...
vmm: initialized successfully
vmm: clone self-test passed
syscall: initialized successfully
userspace: launching ring3 init
user: hello
```

## Known limitations

This release uses an embedded deterministic ELF smoke-test image rather than a disk-backed `/bin/init`. The original v0.4 filesystem is intentionally minimal, fork is eager rather than copy-on-write, and the scheduler is a foundation rather than a complete production process lifecycle. ATA/FAT32 storage, disk-backed exec, blocking wait, and page-by-page user-pointer validation are v0.5 work.

## Contributing

Keep the build freestanding and warning-clean under the repository’s strict `-Werror` flags. Every architecture or syscall change should preserve the `user: hello` regression, include a serial-visible initialization or test marker, and be validated with a clean ISO build and QEMU run. Please document ABI assumptions whenever changing interrupt frames, page tables, process stacks, or user/kernel transitions.
